text.text_excerpt: For a bit of history: In New Orleans, roughly 41,000 people died from yellow fever between 1817 to 1905. St Vincent's (1861) was one of the many orphanages built for the children of these yellow fever victims. In 1995, it was bought and remodeled as a hotel. It definitely has that school/boarding house feel. There's a kitchen and dining area on the lobby floor, along with common areas. Each floor has wrap around balconies that overlook a courtyard. Staying here is a really nice introduction to historic New Orleans. I've stayed here twice. St. Vincent's and I go waaay back. I first stayed there while on family vacation in 2001, and the experience was so memorably awful that we laughed about it for years to come. The air conditioner leaked all night, the carpet smelled of mold, and we uncovered several short curly hairs between the sheets. So why, when I recently revisited NOLA for Mardi Gras, did I dare to stay there again? Well, the price was right, as was the location. I adore the Garden District and this gorgeous old guesthouse happens to be near all its main bragging points, including the St Charles Streetcar. Besides, I've stayed at far worse dumps since then. It makes me sad that this place has taken such a Yelp beating. You should understand before you come that, for the price of this place, it is going to be pretty shitty. Helloooo! I give this place 4 stars solely because I had so much fun when I stayed here. It was one of my very first trips to New Orleans (I had previously stayed at India House Hostel), and I was intoxicated by the city. So old! So quirky! So dirrrty! And I felt like this place was all of those things too. When you first walk in, don't be intimidated by the drug addicted prostitutes and pimps that are buzzing around the front counter. Seriously.
